verses.text: On the twenty-first day of the seventh month, the LORD sent another message through Haggai:
“Tell Judah’s governor Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, the high priest Joshua son of Jehozadak, and everyone else who remains:
‘Who among you remembers how this house looked in its former glory? What does it look like to you now? Doesn’t it seem like nothing beside that?’

“But now be strong, Zerubbabel,” says the LORD. “Be strong, Joshua son of Jehozadak, high priest. Be strong, all you people of the land, and get to work, because I am with you,” says the LORD of Armies.
“This is the promise I made with you when you came out of Egypt. My Spirit remains among you. Don’t be afraid.”
“The LORD of Armies says this: In a little while, I will shake the heavens, the earth, the sea, and the dry land once more.
“I will shake every nation. The treasures of all nations will come, and I will fill this house with glory,” says the LORD of Armies.
“The silver belongs to me, and the gold belongs to me,” says the LORD of Armies.
“The glory of this later house will be greater than the glory of the first,” says the LORD of Armies. “And here in this place I will give peace,” says the LORD of Armies.
On the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month, in Darius’s second year, the LORD gave Haggai another message:
“The LORD of Armies says: Ask the priests what the law teaches.
“If someone carries consecrated meat in a fold of their clothes, and that fold touches bread, stew, wine, oil, or any other food, does the food become holy?” The priests answered, “No.”
Then Haggai asked, “If someone made unclean by touching a dead body touches any of those things, do they become unclean?” The priests answered, “Yes.”
Haggai replied, “That’s how this people and this nation are before me,” says the LORD. “Everything they do, and everything they offer there, is unclean.”
“From this day on, think carefully about what happened before stone was set on stone for the LORD’s temple.
“When someone came to a grain pile expecting twenty measures, there were only ten. When someone came to the wine vat expecting fifty measures, there were only twenty.
“I struck all your work with blight, mildew, and hail, but you still didn’t turn back to me,” says the LORD.
“Think carefully from this day on, from the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month—from the day the foundation of the LORD’s temple was laid. Think it through.
“Is there any seed left in the barn? The vine, fig tree, pomegranate, and olive tree still haven’t produced. But from this day on, I will bless you.”
The LORD sent Haggai a second message that same day:
“Tell Judah’s governor Zerubbabel: I am about to shake the heavens and the earth.
“I will bring down kingdoms and destroy the strength of the nations’ kingdoms. I will overturn their chariots and their drivers. Horses and riders will fall, each by the sword of another.

“On that day,” says the LORD of Armies, “I will take you, Zerubbabel my servant, son of Shealtiel,” says the LORD, “and make you like my signet ring, because I have chosen you,” says the LORD of Armies.
